SAMIN-DURR:44:58/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:58/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:44:58/r1.claim: The pronoun in يسرناه refers to the Qurʾan; بلسانك means “in your language,” with bāʾ of accompaniment.
SAMIN-DURR:44:58/r1.anchor: أي: القرآن بلسانك أي بلغتك. والباء للمصاحبة/

ASAD-NOTES:44:58/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:44:58/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:44:58/r1.claim: God made the revelation understandable in the Prophet's human tongue so people would take it to heart.
ASAD-NOTES:44:58/r1.anchor: easy to understand, in thine own [human] tongue, so that men might take it to heart

ASAD-NOTES:44:58#n34/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:44:58#n34/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:44:58#n34/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to his note 81 on 19:97 for this phrase.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r1.claim: Taysīr means making something suitable for its purpose and firm and sound in every respect.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r1.anchor: means to make something appropriate and suitable for a purpose and to make it firm and sound in all aspects.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r2.claim: He illustrates the sense with preparing a horse for riding by equipping it, and applies the analogy to furnishing the Qur’an for education and reminder.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r2.anchor: to make a horse ready for riding by adorning it with a bridle, saddle, stirrups and other relevant things.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r3.claim: Islahi rejects the view that the verse calls the Qur’an merely easy and bland: its ease serves teaching and reminder, while its comprehensive subject matter includes intricate matters.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r3.anchor: this verse to mean that the Qur’ ān is a very easy and bland book have not been able to grasp the essence of the word.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r4.claim: The Qur’an communicates intricate matters of wisdom to hearts through majestic, inimitable styles, though those matters require deep deliberation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r4.anchor: it has adopted such majestic styles which cannot be emulated by anyone.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r5.claim: Islahi refers readers to his discussion of 19:97 and says he will revisit the issue in his commentary on Sūrah al-Qamar.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r5.anchor: the explanation of verse 97 of S ūrah Maryam

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r6.claim: The Prophet’s tongue is the pure, unadulterated Quraysh dialect, the best archetype of eloquent Arabic; the Prophet exemplifies it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r6.anchor: the pure and unadulterated language of the Quraysh which was the best archetype of eloquent Arabic

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r7.claim: Revelation in the Prophet’s exemplary Quraysh Arabic conclusively communicated the truth; failure to understand it is the hearers’ fault, not the Book’s or Prophet’s.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r7.anchor: to conclusively communicate the truth to the Quraysh, the Almighty has revealed this Book in the language of the Prophet (sws)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r8.claim: The Qur’an aims to remind people of truths granted by intellect and nature, lessons in themselves and the world, and guidance from earlier Prophets, especially Abraham.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r8.anchor: express the purpose of the revelation of the Qur’ ān in a very elaborate and thorough manner: to receive reminder.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r9.claim: The purpose also warns that those who refuse reminder should expect the fate of rebellious people, which their own history recalls.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p246/r9.anchor: if they are not prepared to be reminded, then they should get ready to meet the fate destined by God for such rebellious people.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r3.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r3.claim: An alternative explanation is that God sent the Quran down on Muhammad's tongue rather than in writing because he was unlettered.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r3.anchor: أنزلناه على لسان كبلا كتابة لكونك أميا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r4.claim: This is a concise conclusion to the sura, summing up its preceding detailed exposition and recalling its command to warn by the clear Book.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r4.anchor: ذكرهم بالكتاب المبين فإنما يسرناه بلسانك

ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r5.claim: The purpose is that they understand the Quran, remember through it, and act according to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r5.anchor: كي يفهموه ويتذكروا به ويعملوا بموجبه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r6.claim: If they do not heed it, the Prophet is to await what befalls them; this generalizes the specific warning just given.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p137#3/r6.anchor: أي وإن لم يتذكرواف ما يحلبهم وهو تعميم بعد تخصيص

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#3/r1.claim: God made the Quran easy, with an unspoken object understood from context.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#3/r1.anchor: {فإنما يسرناه} سهلنا القرآن، كناية عن غير مذكور،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#3/r2.claim: The phrase means upon your tongue.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#3/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#3/r6.claim: The Prophet says that whoever recites Ha Mim al-Dukhan at night will have seventy thousand angels seek forgiveness for him by morning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#3/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من قرأ حم الدخان في ليلة أصبح يستغفر له سبعون ألف ملك"

BAYDAWI-FULL:44:57-59/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:57-59/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:57-59/r4.claim: God made the Quran easy by revealing it in the Messenger's language; this summarizes the sura.
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:57-59/r4.anchor: سهلناه حيث أنزلناه بلغتك وهو فذلكة السورة

BAYDAWI-FULL:44:57-59/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:57-59/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:57-59/r5.claim: They may understand it and recall through it what they had not previously recalled.
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:57-59/r5.anchor: لعلهم يفهمونه فيتذكرون به ما لم يتذكروا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r10.claim: The sūrah's conclusion gathers its themes: Qurʾānic blessing, God's creation and oneness, revelation, warnings and past peoples, while disbelievers deny resurrection despite the signs and promises of warning and glad tidings.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r10.anchor: ولما قدم سبحانه في هذه السورة ما للقرآن من البركة بما اشتمل عليه من البشارة والندارة والجمع والفرق , وذكرهم بما يقرون به

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r11.claim: The sūrah's conclusion says God made the Qurʾān greatly easy and accessible.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r11.anchor: سبب عن قوله فذلكة للسورة : { فإنما يسرناه } أي جعلنا له يسرا عظيما وسهولة كبيرة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r12.claim: Because the Prophet was supremely eloquent and unforced, the Qurʾān is associated with his clear Arabic tongue, which addresses Arabs who delight in eloquence.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r12.anchor: وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم أفصح الناس وأبعدهم لذلك من التكلف , أضافه إليه فقط فقال : { بلسانك }

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r13.claim: The hope is that listeners recognize the Qurʾān's inimitability as proof of its teachings on God's oneness and the messenger; eloquent Arabs would otherwise be able to match it.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r13.anchor: { لعلهم يتذكرون } أي ليكونوا عند من يراهم وهو عارف بلسانهم ممن شأنه كشأنهم على رجاء من أن يتذكروا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r14.claim: Remembering God's power, grandeur, and wisdom makes resurrection certain, so that the righteous and corrupt can be distinguished and all people judged.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p85#2/r14.anchor: فإذا تذكروا ذلك مع ما يعرفون من قدرة الملك وكبريائه وحكمته علموا قطعا أنه لا بد من البعث للتمييز بين أهل الصلاح والفساد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r4.claim: The fāʾ presents a summary of the sūra’s aims and their order, returning to the book whose revelation the sūra opened by affirming.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r4.anchor: حيث كان المذكور بعد الفاء فذلكة للسورة ، أي إجمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r5.claim: The pronoun refers to the Qur’an, understood from context and identified with the book named at the sūra’s opening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r5.anchor: وضمير { يسرناه } عائد إلى الكتاب المفهوم من المقام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r6.claim: The fāʾ may introduce the restricted assertion that it was made easy by the Prophet’s tongue, or introduce the goal that they remember, with the prior phrase as setup.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المفرع قوله : { لعلهم يتذكرون } .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r7.claim: Innamā is restriction by reversal: it answers the pagans, who were given an easy path to understanding through eloquence but responded with doubt and mockery.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r7.anchor: والقصر المستفاد من ( إنما ) قصر قلب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r8.claim: The object of yassarnāhu is an omitted noun, understood as its comprehension from context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p320/r8.anchor: فمفعول { يسرناه } مضاف مقدر دل عليه السياق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r1.claim: The bāʾ marks cause: the Qur’an was made easy through the Prophet’s Arabic; the possessive honors him, while the language is that of the Arabs, as each messenger speaks his people’s language.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r1.anchor: والباء في { بلسانك } للسببية ، أي بسبب لغتك ، أي العربية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r2.claim: Calling a language a tongue is a common metaphor: the organ is named for its chief use in speaking.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r2.anchor: وإطلاق اللسان وهو اسم الجارحة المعروفة في الفم على اللغة مجاز شائع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r3.claim: The phrase implies an instruction to keep reminding them through the Qur’an and not tire of their resistance; yassarnāhu means that understanding it was made easy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r3.anchor: والتقدير : فذكرهم به ولا تسأم لعنادهم فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r4.claim: Laʿalla expresses purpose, meaning the Qur’an was made easy so that they might remember, as in another description of the scripture as Arabic.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r5.claim: The concise statement teaches that the Qur’an is easy to understand because its purpose is remembrance, echoing the declaration that it was made easy for remembrance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r5.anchor: وفي هذا الكلام الموجز إخبار بتيسير القرآن للفهم لأن الغرض منه التذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r6.claim: The Qur’an’s eloquence and delivery through the best of messengers make remembrance a natural result, had the audience not been absorbed in doubt and play.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p321/r6.anchor: وبأن سبب ذلك التيسير كونه بأفصح اللغات وكونه على لسان أفضل الرسل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p352#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p352#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p352#2/r1.claim: God made the Quran easy in Arabic so that people might take heed and believe.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p352#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ فإنما يسرناه ﴾ أي سهلناه والكناية عن القرآن ﴿ بلسانك ﴾ أي بلغة العرب ﴿ لعلهم يتذكرون ﴾

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p263/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p263/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p263/r1.claim: God made this Qur'an easy, clear, and plain in the Prophet's language, the most eloquent and lucid language, so people may understand and act on it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p263/r1.anchor: سهلا واضحا بينا جليا بلسانك الذي هو أفصح اللغات وأجلاها وأحلاها وأعلاها

BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r1.claim: The verse is the sura's conclusion and result: God made the manifest Book easy by revealing it in the Prophet's language.

BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r2.claim: Lisān literally means the speech organ and is used here figuratively for language; a Prophetic saying likewise calls Arabic the language of the people of the Jāhiliyya.

BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r3.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r3.claim: The Prophet is quoted describing Arabic as the tongue of the people of the pre-Islamic age; Bursevī cites it as evidence for lisān meaning language.

BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r4.claim: The Qur'an was made easy so the Prophet's people could understand, remember, and act upon it; if they fail, he is to await what befalls them.
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r4.anchor: كي يفهمه قومك ويتذكروا ويعملوا بموجبه وإذا لم يفعلوا ذلك

BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r8.claim: Ease of recitation does not conflict with the Qur'an being a heavy charge (73:5): its language is easy, while its duties are demanding, and reciting is lighter than acting.
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r8.anchor: هو ميسر باللسان وثقيل من حيث اشتماله على التكاليف الشاقة

BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r9.speaker: بعض العرفاء
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r9.claim: An anecdote tells of a scholar whose sick son prompted advice to offer a sacrifice; he chose Qur'an recitation, and a gnostic explained that recitation is on the tongue while giving money is hard because love of wealth is rooted in the heart.
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r9.anchor: إنما أختار القرآن ؛ لأنه في لسانه

BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r10.claim: The wording 'in your tongue' hints that direct hearing of God's speech without an intermediary would overwhelm and kill its hearers, who cannot bear it.
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r10.anchor: فأشار إلى أنه لو أسمعهم كلامه بغير الواسطة لماتوا جميعا

BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r11.speaker: جعفر الصادق
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r11.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says that without God's making it easy, no creature could utter even one letter of the Qur'an.
BURSEVI:v8p334#3/r11.anchor: قال جعفر الصادق رضي الله عنه :

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r1.claim: This verse summarizes the sūra and reminds them through the clear Book.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r2.claim: He made the Qur’an easy by revealing it in the Prophet’s Arabic so his people could understand and remember.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r4.claim: A report promises that one who recites Sūrat Ḥā Mīm al-Dukhān at night will awaken with 70,000 angels seeking forgiveness for him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r4.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1019 ) ( من قرأ سورة حم الدخان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r5.claim: Another report promises forgiveness by morning for one who recites the sūra mentioning the Smoke on Friday night.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p286/r5.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام : ( 1020 ) ( من قرأ سورة حم التي ذكر فيها الدخان في ليلة جمعة

MUQATIL:44:58-59/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:44:58-59/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:44:58-59/r1.claim: God made the Quran easy upon Muhammad's tongue so people might remember and believe in it, though they did not.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p128#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p128#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p128#3/r1.claim: The object made easy is the Book, mentioned at the beginning of the sūra.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p128#3/r1.anchor: اى الكتاب وقد جرى ذكره في اول السورة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p128#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p128#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p128#3/r2.claim: The Qur'an was made easy in the Prophet's language so they might take admonition.

QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r1.claim: The referent is the Quran, made easy in the Prophet's language for him and those who recite it.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r1.anchor: يعني القرآن، أي سهلناه بلغتك عليك وعلى من يقرؤه

QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r2.claim: The purpose is that they take heed, be admonished and refrain from wrongdoing.

QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r3.claim: The wording echoes the verse saying the Quran was made easy for remembrance and asking whether anyone will remember.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r3.anchor: ونظيره: { ولقد يسرنا القرءان للذكر فهل من مدكر }.

QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r4.claim: The sura closes by urging adherence to the Quran, although it is not named explicitly, recalling the opening's statement that revelation came on a blessed night and the verse about its descent on the Night of Decree.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:58-59/r4.anchor: فختم السورة بالحث على اتباع القرآن وإن لم يكن مذكورا، كما قال في مفتتح السورة: إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة

RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r7.claim: The closing verse reiterates the opening description of the Quran as a clear, beneficial Book: God made it easy in Arabic, the Prophet's language, so people may remember.
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r7.anchor: إن ذلك الكتاب المبين ، الكثير الفائدة إنما يسرناه بلسانك ، أي إنما أنزلنا عربيا بلغتك ، لعلهم يتذكرون

RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r8.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r8.claim: Al-Qāḍī takes the verse to show that God intended everyone to believe and know Him and did not intend anyone's unbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r8.anchor: قال القاضي وهذا يدل على أنه أراد من الكل الإيمان والمعرفة وأنه ما أراد من أحد الكفر

RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r9.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r9.claim: Rāzī's school answers that the pronoun in “perhaps they remember” refers to a particular group, which they identify as the believers.
RAZI-FULL:v27p218/r9.anchor: وأجاب أصحابنا أن الضمير في قوله { لعلهم يتذكرون } عائد إلى أقوام مخصوصين فنحن نحمل ذلك على المؤمنين

STUDYQURAN:44:58/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:58/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:44:58/r1.claim: This verse recalls the Quran mentioned in verses 2–3.
STUDYQURAN:44:58/r1.anchor: This verse harkens back to the reference to the Quran in vv. 2–3

STUDYQURAN:44:58/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:58/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:44:58/r2.claim: Its ease upon the Prophet’s tongue partly explains the Quran’s description as a clear Book.
STUDYQURAN:44:58/r2.anchor: That itis easy upon thy tongue explains in part how it is a clear Book (R)

STUDYQURAN:44:58/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:58/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:44:58/r3.claim: This wording resembles Sūrah 54’s repeated refrain that the Quran is made easy to remember.
STUDYQURAN:44:58/r3.anchor: It is similar to the refrain of Sūrah 54: And indeed We have made the Quran easy to remember

STUDYQURAN:44:58/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:58/r4.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:44:58/r4.claim: The Quran’s ease serves its conveyance to others, so they may be admonished and become believers.
STUDYQURAN:44:58/r4.anchor: for the purpose of conveying it to others, that they might be admonished and then become believers (JJ)

SULAMI:v2p238#7/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p238#7/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p238#7/r1.claim: Ibn Ata says God enables remembrance on the tongues of whichever servants He wills, while withholding it from others so they cannot remember Him.
SULAMI:v2p238#7/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : يسره ذكره على لسان من شاء من عباده فلا يفتر عن ذكره بحال وأغلق باب الذكر

TABATABAI:44:57-59/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:57-59/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:57-59/r4.claim: This follows and summarizes everything from the beginning of the sūrah; taysīr means making easy, and the pronoun refers to the Book in the Prophet's Arabic.
TABATABAI:44:57-59/r4.anchor: والضمير للكتاب والمراد بلسان النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم العربية

TABATABAI:44:57-59/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:57-59/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:57-59/r5.claim: God made the Quran's meanings understandable in Arabic so the Prophet's people might remember, similar to 43:3.
TABATABAI:44:57-59/r5.anchor: أي لعل قومك - يتذكرون فتكون الآية قريبة المعنى

TABATABAI:44:57-59/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:57-59/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:44:57-59/r6.claim: Another view says it was made easy to run on the Prophet's tongue, though he was illiterate, as a sign of prophethood; the author says this does not suit the summary context.
TABATABAI:44:57-59/r6.anchor: إجراؤه على لسانه وهو أمي لا يقرأ ولا يكتب ليكون آية لصدق نبوته

TABRISI:44:51-59/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:51-59/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:44:51-59/r12.claim: “As a favor from your Lord” may state the purpose of God's act, be governed by an implied verb meaning “He gave them,” or confirm what preceded as God's favor.
TABRISI:44:51-59/r12.anchor: مفعول له تقديره فعل الله ذلك بهم فضلا منه

TABRISI:44:56-59/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:56-59/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:44:56-59/r13.claim: God made the Qur'an easy on Muhammad's tongue and its recitation easy for him; the pronoun refers to an unstated Qur'an.
TABRISI:44:56-59/r13.anchor: أي سهلنا القرآن فالهاء كناية عن غير مذكور والمعنى هونا القرآن على لسانك

TABRISI:44:56-59/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:56-59/r14.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:44:56-59/r14.claim: Alternatively, God made the Qur'an Arabic so Muhammad and his people could understand it easily.
TABRISI:44:56-59/r14.anchor: وقيل: معناه جعلنا القرآن عربيا ليسهل عليك وعلى قومك تفهمه

TABRISI:44:56-59/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:56-59/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:44:56-59/r15.claim: The purpose is for people to remember the Qur'an's commands, prohibitions, promises, and threats and reflect on them.
TABRISI:44:56-59/r15.anchor: ليتذكروا ما فيه من الأمر والنهي والوعد والوعيد ويتفكروا فيه

THALABI:v8p356/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p356/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p356/r5.claim: In the statement that God made it easy by Muhammad's tongue, the pronoun refers to an unstated Qur'an.
THALABI:v8p356/r5.anchor: فإنما يسرناه سهلناه، كناية عن غير مذكور.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p128/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p128/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p128/r1.claim: Muqatil says God made the Quran easy on Muhammad's tongue.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p128/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني القرآن يقول هوناه على لسانك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p128/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p128/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p128/r2.claim: The purpose was that people take heed and believe, though they did not believe.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p128/r2.anchor: لكي يتعظوا فيؤمنوا به فلم يؤمنوا به

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:44:58-59/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:44:58-59/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:44:58-59/r1.claim: God made the Quran easy in Muhammad's tongue so that people may take admonition.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:44:58-59/r1.anchor: فإنما يسرناه } سهلنا القرآن { بلسانك لعلهم يتذكرون } يتعظون

ELMALILI:44:58-59/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:44:58-59/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:44:58-59/r1.claim: This conclusion summarizes the surah’s opening: God made the manifest Qur’an accessible through the Prophet’s tongue, in clear and easy Arabic alone, so that people may understand and reflect.
ELMALILI:44:58-59/r1.anchor: bu güzel beyânı bu açık ve kolay anlatışı başka bir dil ile değil[^1] yalnız Arapça ile yaptık[^2]

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:58/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:58/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:58/r1.claim: The surah closes by returning to the importance and special qualities of the Qur'an and urging people to turn to it for understanding and reflection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:58/r1.anchor: Sûre, Kur’an’ın önemine dikkat çekerek başlamış, yeri geldikçe onun müstesna niteliklerine temas etmişti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:58/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:58/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:58/r2.claim: The Qur'an is easy to understand because it was revealed in the Prophet's people's language and has no tangled expressions or concepts beyond its audience.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:58/r2.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in kavmiyle konuşup anlaştığı dilde vahyedilmiştir, içinde hedef kitlenin anlamakta güçlük çekecekleri çetrefil ifade ve kavramlar yoktur

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r3.claim: The closing section presents the Qur'an's clear Arabic revelation as a favor to Quraysh, echoing the sūrah's opening praise and affirming that it fully conveys the truth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r3.anchor: the sūrah began with a note on the exaltedness of the Qur’ ān and it ends on the same note. In it, the Quraysh are warned that the Almighty has equipped the Qur’ ān with all essential requisites

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r4.claim: Rejecting this favor brings the fate of those who rejected God's messengers; if they choose to await punishment, the Prophet is told to await their evil day too.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r4.anchor: if instead of benefiting from this favour, these people want to wait for the punishment, then he too should wait for the advent of this evil day for them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r3.claim: The coming section identifies disbelief in life after death as the cause of Quraysh rebellion and heedlessness of the future.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r3.anchor: the real reason for the rebelliousness of the Quraysh is highlighted: they do not imagine that there is life after this worldly existence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r4.claim: The section first offers intellectual and natural arguments for reward and punishment, then describes the fate of believers and disbelievers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r4.anchor: first the intellectual and natural arguments which substantiate the law of reward and punishment are cited. After this, the fate of both the believers and the disbelievers is depicted.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r4.claim: The sūrah closes by returning to its opening theme: the Qur’an’s exaltedness as a great favour to the Arabs, whose valuation of it brings success while arrogance brings destruction; the intervening argument established its truth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r4.anchor: sūrah began with the mention of the Qur’ ān’s exaltedness: it is indeed a great favour which the Almighty has blessed the Arabs with.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r5.claim: Like examples in earlier sūrahs, an eloquent orator closes by recalling the opening topic, giving the audience a complete final reminder.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r5.anchor: An orator generally ends his speech by reminding the audience of the topic with which he began it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r6.claim: The opening particle fa connects this verse with the subject of the preceding sections.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p245/r6.anchor: The letter فindicates the affinity with the subject of the previous sections

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r5.claim: The pronoun in “We made it easy” refers to the Qur'an, and “in your tongue” means in your language, an Arab language.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p409/r5.anchor: والضمير في يسرناه عائد على القرآن وبلسانك: بلغتك، وهي لغة لعرب
